concepts.name: Table 2.6: sessions of the Constituent Assembly
concepts.description: Dates and periods of the eleven sessions and the final meeting.
concepts.idea: The Assembly held eleven sessions from December 1946 to November 1949.
concepts.rule: Table 2.6: First Session 9-23 December 1946; Second 20-25 January 1947; Third 28 April-2 May 1947; Fourth 14-31 July 1947; Fifth 14-30 August 1947; Sixth 27 January 1948; Seventh 4 November 1948-8 January 1949; Eighth 16 May-16 June 1949; Ninth 30 July-18 September 1949; Tenth 6-17 October 1949; Eleventh 14-26 November 1949. The Assembly met once more on 24 January 1950 when members signed the Constitution.
concepts.example: The Seventh Session, from 4 November 1948, saw the introduction of the final draft.

concepts.name: Experts Committee of the Congress and important facts about the Assembly
concepts.description: The 1946 Experts Committee, its work and other facts on officers and calligraphy.
concepts.idea: The Congress Experts Committee of 1946 prepared material for the Assembly.
concepts.rule: On 8 July 1946 the Congress appointed an Experts Committee under Nehru with M. Asaf Ali, K.M. Munshi, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.T. Shah, D.R. Gadgil, Humayun Kabir and K. Santhanam; Krishna Kripalani was co-opted as member and convener. It met in New Delhi (20-22 July 1946) and Bombay (15-17 August 1946), discussed Assembly procedure, committees and a draft resolution on objectives. Granville Austin said it set India on the road to her present Constitution. Other facts: the Assembly's symbol was the elephant; Sir B.N. Rau was constitutional adviser; H.V.R. Iyengar was Secretary; S.N. Mukherjee was chief draftsman; Prem Behari Narain Raizada was calligrapher; Nand Lal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha decorated it; Vasant Krishan Vaidya did the Hindi calligraphy.
concepts.example: Beohar Rammanohar Sinha illuminated the original Preamble.
